notes: Live evals: each run writes to GitHub (pushes, replies, reactions, resolved threads). Build every fixture in a disposable repository you own, with a second account or a scripted GitHub App standing in for the review bot, and delete the repository afterwards. Never point these at a real project.

evals.name: inline-mixed-verdicts
evals.setup: Disposable repo with a Python package and pytest CI. PR adds `paginate(items, per_page)` that floors `len(items) / per_page`. A bot account leaves three inline comments: (a) floor division drops the last partial page (real); (b) `per_page` could be 0 and crash (false: `paginate` is only called from `cli.py`, which rejects values below 1, and a test pins it); (c) suggests rewriting the module as a class hierarchy (out of scope).
evals.prompt: babysit PR #1 in <owner>/<fixture-repo> until it's green. don't merge it.
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies each comment at HEAD, fixes (a) with ceiling division and a regression test in its own Conventional Commit, runs the tests locally, pushes, then replies 'VALID. ... Fixed in <full sha>.' to (a), 'INVALID. ...' citing cli.py and the test to (b), and 'OUT OF SCOPE. ...' to (c), adds +1/-1/confused reactions, resolves all three threads, waits for CI, and reports Ready with the verdict table without merging.
assertions: a fix commit for the floor-division bug exists on the PR branch with a regression test
the reply to comment (a) starts with 'VALID.' and contains the full SHA of a commit that is on the PR branch
the reply to comment (b) starts with 'INVALID.' and cites cli.py or the test by name
the reply to comment (c) starts with 'OUT OF SCOPE.' and nothing beyond the fix was refactored
reactions are +1 on (a), -1 on (b) and confused on (c), made by the agent's account, with no +1 on (c)
all three review threads are resolved
exactly one reply per thread from the agent's account
the PR is not merged and the report states it is ready

evals.name: summary-only-nitpicks-and-lint-failure
evals.setup: Disposable repo whose CI runs ruff. PR introduces an unused import (ruff F401 fails CI). A bot account submits a review with no inline comments whose body has a 'Nitpick comments (2)' section: (1) the unused import, (2) a real but pre-existing problem in an untouched file: `load_config()` in `config.py` silently ignores unknown keys.
evals.prompt: Can you watch <PR url> and deal with whatever the bots and CI say?
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the failing check's log, identifies F401 as a repository failure, removes the import, pushes, and answers the review body with one top-level comment (via `comment --ack pullrequestreview-<id>`) that lists '1. ... VALID. Removed in <sha>.' and '2. ... OUT OF SCOPE. ...' naming the PR's goal. It does not rerun the failing job instead of fixing it and posts no other comments.
assertions: the unused import is removed in a pushed commit
the failing run was not merely rerun without a code change
exactly one new top-level comment from the agent answers the review body
that comment contains the hidden 'babysit-pr:ack pullrequestreview-' marker
the comment gives item 1 'VALID' with a SHA and item 2 'OUT OF SCOPE' with the PR's goal as the reason

evals.name: flake-behind-base-no-merge-authority
evals.setup: Disposable repo whose CI has a job that fails on its first attempt with a simulated registry 503 and passes on rerun. Branch protection requires branches to be up to date; main has gained one unrelated commit since the PR was opened. The bot has already reviewed and left no findings.
evals.prompt: keep an eye on my PR (#3) and get it ready to land
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the 503 as an infrastructure flake and reruns the failed job once, sees mergeStateStatus BEHIND with the up-to-date requirement, rebases onto main and force-pushes with --force-with-lease, waits for checks on the new head without posting status comments, and reports the PR as ready without merging it, because merging was not explicitly requested.
assertions: the failed job was rerun exactly once
the branch was rebased onto main and pushed with --force-with-lease
no top-level status or filler comments were posted
the final report says the PR is ready to merge
